items.title: Louis Tio Interview, 1960-10-26
items.q: And also there's Eddie Sherry, he played with the Chicago police band. Remember him? Yeah, he's the one.

ctx.x: He was the pupil of your brother's.

That's right. He was a, he had a barbershop here on Liberty in Byron. He, he, he taken lessons from my brother and he was made famous. He went to Chicago and he stayed in Chicago. And also there's Eddie Sherry, he played with the Chicago police band. Remember him? Yeah, he's the one.

items.title: Louis Tio Interview, 1960-10-26
items.q: Like a fellow like Eddasharie, he was a Baba. He had to, used to come twice a week, sometimes, sometimes once a week.

ctx.x: Did most of the pupils come more than once a week or how often would they have lessons, do you know?

Well, it's a cause. Some of them come, that's a cause in the door. They had some of them that was working and they wasn't able to make it once a week. Some of them used to come twice a week. Yes. Like a fellow like Eddasharie, he was a Baba. He had to, used to come twice a week, sometimes, sometimes once a week. It's according to how his business was going.
Oh, by the way, before I forget, did your uncles and your brother have another trade besides their music? Did they, somebody told me one of them was a cigar maker at Breeders?
